name: Ari
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Read full scanned text of Reesink 1976, Languages of the Aramia River Area (PL A-45, ANU repository): Ari section is sociolinguistic notes plus wordlist comparison with Gogodala; no phonology or stress statement.

sources.citation: van Tongeren, Charlotte. 2023. A grammar of Suki (PhD thesis, ANU), sec. 1.2.1 p. 11; Voorhoeve, C.L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages, PL C-38: 345-459
sources.note: Checked as closest-relative sources: van Tongeren p. 11 only notes Waruna 'possibly.. the same variety as Ari (Reesink 1976: 9)'; Voorhoeve 1975 never mentions Ari (its p. 354 'stress is phonemic' concerns Gogodala, p. 352 first-syllable stress concerns Suki). Neither says anything about Ari stress.

sources.citation: Reesink, Ger P. 1976. Languages of the Aramia River area. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 19 (Pacific Linguistics A-45), 1-37. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-A45.1
sources.note: Sec. 3 'Ari' pp. 7-10 (sociolinguistic notes, lexicostatistics vs Gogodala/Suki/Waruna, Chart 5 loanwords/cognates) and sec. 3.3 'Notes on phonology and grammar' pp. 9-10 give only a 'very tentative' phoneme inventory (consonants p t k b d g mb nd ngg m n s r w y; vowels i e a o u, e/E and o/O status uncertain); wordlists pp. 8-9 and 31-34. Nothing at all on stress, accent or tone.

104 lexical items, all sourced to Reesink 1976; no other source listed; nothing on stress.

sources.note: Population 50 (2000 S. Wurm); Ari and Serea villages; dialect Serea; also use Gogodala; 'nearly extinct'. Nothing on phonology.
Phoneme table derived from Reesink 1976 only; no mention of stress.
